sources.title: Associates Program Operating Agreement
sources.what_was_checked: §5 requires the statement 'As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.' to be clearly and prominently stated on the Site. §6 says violating §5 is a material breach. Read: chunks 0–1 of 4.

sources.title: Associates Program Policies (Commission Income Statement)
sources.what_was_checked: §2 lists disqualified purchases including (c) prohibited paid-search placements on Amazon marks, (d) referral by a link generated or displayed on a search engine, (e) a 'Redirecting Link' that sends users indirectly via an intermediate site without a customer action, and (g) purchases not correctly tracked because links are improperly formatted. §1 defines a 24-hour session and an 89-day cart window. Read: chunks 0–1 of 11. The remaining chunks were not read.

sources.title: Qualify your outbound links to Google
sources.what_was_checked: rel="sponsored" marks advertisements or paid placements; values can be combined with other rel values.
used_for: rel="sponsored" on every outbound product link

sources.title: 16 CFR Part 255 — Guides Concerning Use of Endorsements and Testimonials in Advertising
sources.publisher: U.S. Federal Trade Commission, via eCFR (authoritative but unofficial)
sources.version_stated: Up to date as of 11/18/2026; source 88 FR 48102 (July 26, 2023)
sources.what_was_checked: §255.5: a material connection between endorser and seller that the audience does not expect must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously; affiliate compensation is named as an example. 'Clear and conspicuous' definition: difficult to miss and easily understandable. The eCFR page was checked for citation and the Part 255 table of contents; the §255.5 text came from an eCFR search excerpt.
